topic: Stateless chat APIs: every turn resends the whole history, so chatbot input cost grows with conversation length
text:
Your chatbot doesn't remember the conversation. You resend it on every single turn.

Chat APIs like Anthropic's Messages API are stateless: you pass the prior turns in the messages parameter and the model writes the next one. OpenAI's docs say the same about chained responses: all previous input tokens in the chain are billed as input tokens.

A quick illustration, assuming each turn adds about 200 tokens:
• Turn 1 sends ~200 tokens
• Turn 10 sends ~2,000
• Turn 50 sends ~10,000

Add them up and a 50-turn chat has billed roughly 255,000 input tokens, not 10,000. Cost grows with the square of the length, and the history also eats the context window.

My rule of thumb: cap history, summarize older turns, and put the stable system prompt first so prompt caching can discount it.

How do you trim long chat histories in your bots: sliding window, summaries, or something else?
